properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): Anthony saw `[workspace.package] version = "0.74.0"` with v0.76.0 released — every cut DID bump the version; he was reading the main reflow2 checkout, parked since 2026-09-28 on #620's merged branch 24 commits behind main, and nothing reports a checkout that has fallen behind
properties.source: RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh) on Anthony's /root-cause, dev_reflow2 hub session, 2026-10-01/02; `git show <ref>:Cargo.toml` for origin/main, every tag v0.70.0–v0.76.0 and origin/cut-v0.77.0; `git status -sb` and `git log -1` in /home/ajs7/project/reflow2
properties.statement:
① OBSERVED, as Anthony pasted it: `[workspace.package] version = "0.74.0" … rust-version = "1.94"`, with the question "this is past version 0.74.0 … why this wasn't updated properly with each version we've released?". Expected: the current version. NOT affected: origin/main reads 0.76.0.

② PRECEDENT:
- cap:a-cut-moves-every-version-claim-together, plus every cut's accept event (e.g. the v0.74.0 cut's "0.73.0 → 0.74.0 … check_doc_versions: 11 claims agree").
- flo2's fact:the-served-binary-is-not-the-repo-2026-09-14: "developed here" never means "latest". Same class, other side.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) a cut skipped the bump; (b) a different Cargo.toml was read; (c) the observation is right but the file read is not main.

④/⑤ MEASURED. `[workspace.package] version` at each ref:
- v0.70.0 0.70.0, v0.71.0 0.71.0, v0.72.0 0.72.0, v0.73.0 0.73.0, v0.74.0 0.74.0, v0.75.0 0.75.0, v0.76.0 0.76.0;
- origin/main 0.76.0, origin/cut-v0.77.0 0.77.0.
(a) is REFUTED. (c) holds: /home/ajs7/project/reflow2 is on `fix/a-degraded-server-recovers-when-its-cause-clears` (#620, merged 2026-10-01), "[behind 24]", HEAD 4659832 dated 2026-09-28 18:20, and its Cargo.toml reads 0.74.0. It also holds an uncommitted edit to temporal_tools.rs: an early draft of the manual_work_ledger bound, which shipped differently as #638.

⑥ THE CLASS: a working checkout serves as "reflow2" for people AND for tools, and nothing keeps it on main or says when it falls behind. The same night it caused three things:
- Anthony reading 0.74.0;
- the live child-reflow2 store, which auto-exports into that checkout and tracks its branch, lagging main by 169 nodes (6,115 against 6,284);
- the hub's reflow2 watch reading that lagging export, until it was moved to a clean worktree.
A version bump cannot fix any of these. The checkout has to be brought back to main, and the live store resynced, or nothing will say so next time.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED:
- which session left the checkout there (the 2026-09-28 session started the ledger fix in place, then moved it to a worktree, by inference);
- whether any other tool reads that checkout's files as current.
Bringing it back is not done: the live store has to be resynced with main at the same time, or its next auto-export overwrites main's export in the working tree with the lagging design.
